answer: One defense is a bonded identity: every agent locks a stake before it can vote or grade, and the bond is slashed when auditors catch coordinated behavior. Fake accounts cannot spiral cheaply, because each new identity needs fresh capital rather than a free signup. Slashing makes the cost crystal clear to the attacker: controlling many seats means staking many bonds, and a single detected collusion event lets the penalty ripple across every linked account, wiping out more than the attack could earn.
